rows.title: Aviator Transmission Safety Recalls: Park and Direction-Control Defects
rows.howToFix: Check the VIN in the NHTSA and Lincoln/Ford recall systems and follow the instructions for the campaign actually open. For 26V402, follow the current do-not-drive advisory and contact a Lincoln dealer for transport guidance; the free remedy is updated PCM software plus inspection and replacement of damaged park-system components as needed. For 23S06, the dealer inspects for the loose bolt and replaces the transmission if the inspection fails. For 25S19, the dealer replaces the transmission main-control valve body. Do not buy transmission parts or combine a harsh-shift complaint with these recall remedies without VIN confirmation.

rows.title: 12-Volt Battery Drain from Third-Party App Modem Activity
rows.howToFix: Identify and uninstall any non-Ford/Lincoln app that accesses the vehicle, then fully charge and test the 12-volt battery and monitor key-off draw and battery state of charge. If symptoms remain, follow normal Ford battery, battery-monitoring-sensor, charging-system, modem, and module network-sleep diagnostics. A Deep Sleep notification by itself is not a failed module; if state of charge does not change after charging or a BMS reset, continue the battery/BMS diagnostic path. Do not replace a latch, TCU, battery, or other module without a failed test, and do not present a maintainer as the repair for an unresolved drain.

rows.title: Fuel Tank Puncture and Fire Risk in Rear Impacts (Livery/Limousine Shield Program)
rows.howToFix: Have the Ford TSB performed (grind the stabilizer-bar bracket tab flush) and install the Ford rear-axle fuel tank shield kit, which was offered free to Town Car limousine/livery operators and costs roughly $100 in parts for civilian cars. Verify with a dealer whether the shield was ever installed.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: Verify with a dealer whether the shield was ever installed.

rows.title: Lighting Control Module (LCM) Failure — Headlights Cut Out
rows.howToFix: Replace the LCM or send it to a board-level rebuild service (around $150-250) that replaces the failure-prone relays and re-flows the solder joints; rebuilds keep the module's VIN programming. On 2003-2005 cars, the bypass-module kit Ford developed for recall 15S39 on Crown Victoria/Grand Marquis addresses the same headlamp relay circuit.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Plastic Intake Manifold Coolant Crossover Failure (Class-Action Defect)
rows.howToFix: Replace the manifold with the revised design (DuPont Zytel composite with an aluminum front coolant crossover, used from mid-2001/2002 onward; Dorman and Ford service parts both use the aluminum crossover). Replace any coolant-soaked coils and pressure-test the system afterward.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: Replace any coolant-soaked coils and pressure-test the system afterward.

rows.title: Coil-on-Plug Ignition Coil Failure and Misfires (4.6L V8)
rows.howToFix: Diagnose by swapping the suspect coil to another cylinder and confirming the misfire code follows; replace failed coils and boots, and replace high-mileage spark plugs at the same time. If coolant is found in a plug well, fix the intake manifold leak first or the new coil will fail too.

rows.title: Power Window Regulator Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the regulator assembly (aftermarket units are inexpensive; many include the motor) through the inner door panel — a roughly one-hour job per door at an independent shop. Forum guides cover DIY replacement on 1998-2002 doors in detail.

rows.title: Town Car Rear Air Suspension Bag/Compressor Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace bags as a pair ($300-$600 aftermarket installed). Compressor + dryer kit ~$200-$400 installed. Many owners convert to coil springs with a Strutmasters-style kit (~$300-$500) — loses self-leveling but no further maintenance. Limo owners need to keep air for headroom adjustment.

rows.title: Town Car HVAC Blend Door Actuator Clicking / No-Heat
rows.howToFix: Replacement blend door actuator ($30-$80 part) — labor varies wildly by which actuator. Driver side: 30 min. Passenger side: 1-2 hours. Floor/defrost actuator (deepest): 3-5 hours. Aftermarket Dorman actuators have mixed reviews — Motorcraft OEM lasts longer.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: Power Steering Rack and Line Leaks (2003+ Rack-and-Pinion)
rows.howToFix: Replace the leaking component: a damaged O-ring or high-pressure line is a cheap fix, while a leaking rack is normally replaced with a remanufactured unit followed by a front toe alignment. Flush old fluid and verify the pump was not run dry.

rows.title: Steering Intermediate Shaft Corrosion — Loss of Steering (Recall 13V-385)
rows.howToFix: Have a Ford/Lincoln dealer perform recall 13V-385 free of charge: replace the lower intermediate shaft, inspect and repair the upper shaft and column lower bearing, and install a retainer clip if the bearing has separated. Check the VIN for open recall status; out-of-scope cars need the shafts replaced at a shop.
